subject: Reserved capacity commit — staggered activation & market-price ceiling/floor
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena@atlas.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasAI Procurement <procurement@atlas.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — initial ask

Hi Nikhil / Kimberly,

Thanks for the proposal packet. AtlasAI is excited to move to a reserved capacity model with Redwood for Q3–Q4 inference needs. Quick summary of where we landed internally:
- Target committed GPU hours: equivalent to 120 A100-days per month (we understand Redwood maps to Aurora SKUs).
- We prefer a staggered activation: 40 A100-days/mo active immediately, +40 in month 3, +40 in month 6, to smooth cashflow.
- Critical asks from procurement: a pricing collar tied to an external GPU index (sudden market swings are our concern). We want a floor and ceiling on unit pricing plus a quarterly reconciliation.

Attached is a redline SOW and a simple pricing workbook (pricing-model-staggered.xlsx) showing our preferred collar: +/-15% off the baseline, with a mechanism for pass-through of extreme moves (>25%).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a staggered activation schedule and the proposed collar mechanics? Also, please flag any approval path we need for an upfront discount (Atlas is requesting a 22% discount on list for a 12-month committed term).

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Partnerships
AtlasAI

Attachments: Atlas_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing-model-staggered.xlsx

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@atlas.ai>, AtlasAI Procurement <procurement@atlas.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — staggered activation & pricing collar

Elena / Carlos — thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. We can support staggered activation (phased provisioning) and a price-collar style mechanism, but there are a few operational and finance constraints to iron out: 

1) Staggered activation: we can schedule tranche activations at months 0 / 3 / 6. There will be a short provisioning lead (1–2 weeks) per tranche for Dedicated pools; we will include a tranche ramp credit for any provisioning delay beyond agreed activation dates.

2) Price collar: Redwood is open to a floor/ceiling tied to a shared GPU-market index, but our standard legal/finance ask is: the collar should be calculated on a per-quarter basis with explicit trigger thresholds and a reconciliation invoice (positive or negative) within 30 days. For market moves >25% we propose an automatic pass-through clause (customer pays the delta above the ceiling or Redwood issues credit below the floor).

3) Discount request: 22% off list for a 12-month commit is outside of my direct approval band. I'll need a finance sign-off for an effective blended discount at that level given the tranche phasing and the collar exposure. Marcus — can you weigh in on discount posture and whether a contingency escrow (partial refund if GPU index falls) helps structure this?

Will route a short summary to finance and legal once we agree the collar math. For transparency I'm attaching the draft commit term (commit-term-draft.docx) with placeholders for collar parameters.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to review discount/escrow options (internal) — target EOD tomorrow.
- Kimberly to confirm operational SLA language around tranche provisioning.
- Elena to confirm final collar numbers you prefer (+/-15% vs +/-10%).

Thanks — Nikhil
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Reserved capacity proposal — staggered activation & pricing collar

Nikhil / Kim — reviewed Atlas's collar ask and the 22% discount request. High level:

- Discount: 22% blended off list for a 12-month term with a 120 A100-day equivalent commit is aggressive but achievable if we bifurcate the economics: a base (committed) price at ~15% discount and an additional performance/usage milestone rebate of up to 7% tied to attainment (run-rate, no-shows on tranches). That reduces upfront exposure.

- Collar mechanics: I prefer a dual-trigger approach: a quarterly recalculation using a published GPU index (we can reference third-party index X) AND a 30-day resolution window. For swings between 15–25% we settle by credit/charge applied to the next invoice; beyond 25% triggers an executive review and automatic pass-through.

- Escrow / contingency: recommend a small escrow (2–4% of committed value) held for the first two tranches to offset extreme downward price moves; if index falls below floor at reconciliation, we release escrow as credit to Redwood and adjust forward invoices. This is simpler than refunding large historical invoices.

I'll support a bundled approval: finance and revenue operations can approve the 15% base plus rebate structure and the collar up to +/-15% without exec sign-off. Anything increasing pass-through exposure beyond that needs VP approval.

If we present the escrow + milestone-rebate structure to Atlas, we should be able to land near their 22% ask without open-ended exposure.

-Marcus
Director, Revenue Operations

Attachments referenced: pricing-model-staggered.xlsx (internal copy with modeled rebate flows)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@atlas.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@atlas.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit — staggered activation & market-price ceiling/floor (approval path)

Elena / Carlos — thanks for patience while we reviewed internally. Short version of where Redwood can land (pending legal terms in SOW):

1) Pricing & discount: base committed price = list - 15% (applies to all committed tranches). Up to 7% additional rebate is available by meeting tranche activation and usage milestones (detailed in attached pricing-model-staggered.xlsx). Net possible discount = 22% if all milestones are met.

2) Collar and reconciliation: we accept a quarterly collar +/-15% tied to ThirdPartyGPUIndex-X with a 30-day reconciliation invoice. For quarterly swings >25% the contract triggers an automatic pass-through (customer pays delta above ceiling) and an executive notification to both parties; we will use a 2–4% escrow against committed value for the first two tranches to mitigate short-term exposure.

3) Staggered activation: Redwood will provision tranches at months 0/3/6. If provisioning delay >14 days beyond the agreed activation date, Atlas receives a pro-rata tranche credit as outlined in the SOW.

4) Approvals: Marcus has clearance to approve the 15% base + rebate structure and the collar up to +/-15%. Anything increasing pass-through or removing the escrow requires VP-level approval (CC'd Neha).

Next steps:
- Elena: confirm you accept the escrow and the milestone rebate structure so we can finalize SOW redlines.
- Atlas procurement: send preferred DocuSign contact; legal will circulate a commit term with collar language embedded.
- Kimberly: I'll schedule an ops sync to lock provisioning SLA details.

If you want, we can run a quick 20-minute call tomorrow to finalize numbers.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit-term-draft.docx
